chapter: Postwar years, accident and lean times
title: Working a Phillipsburg, Quebec hotel with a trio around 1950
summary: Pinned down to 1949-50, he led a trio at a hotel near Montreal for $50-60 a week plus room and board, sending cash home to his wife during the lean years.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: I have a note here, Herman. It says in the late 1940's you spent a lot of time in Canada, and had your own group in Canada. Is that right?
No.
No?
No, not in Canada. No. I was there with the Saints and Sinners in Canada.

Well this is -- no, we're talking about the forties. Not the sixties. Right after World War II. I'm trying to get that part sort of straightened out. You came back from Philadelphia. You gigged around New York for a while. This was the be-bop period. Things were kind of tough, as you say. And what happened -- let's get into the 1950's. Do you relate anything to the 1950's?
Well, yes, that's when I got hurt, got the automobile accident.
That was --
I had a trio.
Ah, that was the year 1950, wasn't it?
Aaahhh! Oh Canada! You're right.
Right. Right. Okay --
You are right.
Now.
You're right.
Now, relate to that, now, had you been in Canada when you had the accident?
It happened on my -- on my way back. I had been there before.
Okay, well now let's talk about how you got to Canada that time, before you came back.
Right. Well --
What were you doing in Canada before the accident?
Well we hadn't been before '49, or [PltHsburg]? something like that, we'd been up to Phillipsburg. That's about 55 or 60 miles, on this side of -- uh, Montreal.
South of Montreal.
South of Montreal, near -- near -- uh, uh, uh, state of -- near Vermont.
Vermont, toward the -- oh yes. Down toward Vermont.
Yeah.
When you say we, who's we? In this case.
Well I had a trio. I had a piano player. He was driving when I got hurt, broke my hip.
How did you happen to have a job in Phillipsburg, Canada?
Well, it was one of those things when --
that's -- other depression had person would start there, there's no jobs, and nothing for a guy to do, so you had to go out and grab anything you could grab to try to survive!
So -- excuse me.
I was going to say, were you gigging around Canada with this trio, or did you have --
No, no. We worked in a hotel, hotel.
Oh.
And they were paying you -- oh, a lousy 50 or $60.00 a week, and with room and board. So --
How long did you stay at the hotel?
Oh, a year and something, maybe a little more, in there.
A long -- a long --
Yeah, uh-huh. Yeah. So I would stay there and play, and what money -- cash money I got I sent it back here for my wife. To pay bills, with
